stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n}}{16^{n}(2n + 1)} x^{2 n + 1} \) for all \( x \) where the series converges. The series for \( f'(x) \) is obtained by differentiating the series for \( f \) term by term. Find the radius of convergence of the series for \( f'(x) \).

worked_solution.text: Apply the ratio test to the series for \( f \): the ratio of consecutive terms has limit \( \frac{|x|^{2}}{16} \) as \( n \to \infty \), since every factor that is polynomial in \( n \) has ratio tending to 1.
The series for \( f \) converges when \( |x|^{2} < 16 \), that is \( |x| < 4 \), so its radius of convergence is \( 4 \).
Differentiating a power series term by term does not change its radius of convergence, so the series for \( f'(x) \) also has radius \( 4 \).
